prompt:
Research Canonical's official statement on how long an Ubuntu LTS release receives standard support, and how long with Ubuntu Pro / ESM. Cite Canonical's own page and quote the periods.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on Canonical's official documentation, here is the breakdown of Ubuntu LTS support periods.

An Ubuntu LTS release receives **5 years of standard security maintenance** for packages in the Main repository at no cost. This period can be extended to **10 years** for the Main repository and, depending on the subscription, the Universe repository through the **Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM)** service included with Ubuntu Pro. An optional **Legacy add-on** can further extend this to a total of **15 years** of security coverage and support.

Here are the specific claims and their sources:

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance." | CLAIM: Standard support for an LTS release lasts for 5 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/esm | QUOTE: "Ubuntu LTS gained popularity due to a 5-year security maintenance commitment for the operating system (specifically all packages in the 'main repository')." | CLAIM: The free 5-year commitment is specifically for packages in the Main repository.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "ESM extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the 'Main' repository and also adds 10 years of security coverage for the 'Universe' repository." | CLAIM: ESM provides 10 years of security coverage for both Main and Universe repositories.

SOURCE: https://canonical.com/legal/ubuntu-pro-description | QUOTE: "Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM): an additional scope of security patching service... [that] covers fixes to High and Critical CVE for 10 years" | CLAIM: ESM provides an additional 10 years of security patching.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "At the end of the 10 year ESM period, the Legacy add-on can be purchased to cover additional 5 years... giving a total of 15 years security maintenance and support for LTS releases." | CLAIM: The Legacy add-on extends total coverage to 15 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/esm | QUOTE: "Extend the lifetime of your favorite Linux and the open source you use on top with reliable security maintenance for up to 15 years." | CLAIM: Total possible security maintenance with all offerings is up to 15 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/pro/docs/services-overview/ | QUOTE: "ESM infra: this stream expands the scope of security maintenance for Ubuntu LTS releases for packages in the Ubuntu Main repository from 5 years to 10 years;" | CLAIM: ESM-infra specifically extends Main repository support from 5 to 10 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/pro/docs/services-overview/ | QUOTE: "ESM apps: this stream expands the scope of security maintenance to include packages in the Ubuntu Universe repository for the full 10 years of an Ubuntu LTS release’s lifecycle." | CLAIM: ESM-apps provides 10 years of security coverage for the Universe repository.
